claims.statement: The anchor account sent 8 payments to 8 different counterparties in 6 currencies over a 50-hour window, all via ACH.
Each of the 8 counterparties received exactly one transfer from the anchor account and has no other transfers with it.
The anchor account's only external incoming transfer was a small EUR 83.45 cash deposit; all other activity consists of self-transfers that are currency conversions paired with the outbound payments.

findings.narrative: The anchor account 7675/8093BA230 sent 8 ACH payments to 8 different counterparties over a 50-hour window in 6 currencies (USD, EUR, INR, CAD), triggering the fan-out detector (threshold: 6 counterparties in 96 hours). The account's history shows only one incoming external transfer (EUR 83.45 cash) and 8 self-transfers that are currency conversions (EUR to USD, INR, CAD) paired with each outbound payment. Each counterparty received exactly one payment from this anchor and has independent transaction histories with many other parties. The amounts vary widely (USD 1,338 to CAD 22,304) and are not structured. The pattern is consistent with a business or individual making legitimate multi-currency vendor payments, not money laundering.
